youtube.title: 🔥 OpenAI Just Dropped This for Claude Code
youtube.description: Stop context-switching between Claude Code and Codex just to get a code review. OpenAI released an official plugin that brings Codex reviews directly into your Claude Code workflow. You get slash commands for normal reviews, adversarial reviews that challenge your design, and even the ability to delegate entire debugging tasks to Codex in the background. It works with your existing ChatGPT subscription or API key, uses your local Codex install, and picks up your existing config. No separate runtime, no extra account needed. The adversarial review mode is especially powerful because it pressure-tests your implementation choices and asks whether a different approach would have been safer or simpler. Next time you're about to ship, just type /codex:review --background and let it run while you keep coding. Your workflow stays in Claude, but you get Codex-quality reviews without leaving your editor.

linkedin.text:
🚨 You're losing review quality every time you skip the Codex pass because switching tools breaks your flow.

Most devs using Claude Code want Codex reviews, but the context switch kills momentum. You finish a feature in Claude, then manually copy context over to Codex, wait for the review, then come back. By the time you're done, you've lost 20 minutes and your train of thought.

OpenAI just released an official plugin that solves this. It's called Codex plugin for Claude Code, and it brings Codex reviews directly into your existing workflow with slash commands.

Here's what you get:
✅ /codex:review runs a full Codex review without leaving Claude Code
✅ /codex:adversarial-review pressure-tests your design and challenges your implementation choices
✅ /codex:rescue delegates entire debugging tasks to Codex in the background while you keep working

It works with your existing ChatGPT subscription or API key. No separate runtime, no extra account, and it picks up your existing Codex config automatically. The adversarial review mode is especially powerful because it questions whether a different approach would have been safer or simpler, not just whether your code has bugs.

⭐ The repo is brand new from OpenAI and already getting traction from devs who were manually juggling both tools.

Search "openai codex-plugin-cc" on GitHub and check the README for the full command list. What's your biggest friction point when switching between AI coding tools?
